front: Qu'est-ce que tu fais pendant ton temps libre ?
pronunciation: [kehs-kuh tü feh pahn-dahn tohn tahn LEE-bruh]
back: What do you do in your free time?
context: 'Le temps libre' = free time. 'Les loisirs' = leisure activities.

front: Je joue au foot le dimanche.
back: I play soccer on Sundays.
context: 'Jouer à' + sport or game: jouer au foot, au tennis, aux cartes.

front: Elle joue du piano depuis l'enfance.
back: She has played the piano since childhood.
context: 'Jouer de' + instrument: jouer du piano, de la guitare, du violon.

front: Je fais de la natation deux fois par semaine.
pronunciation: [zhuh feh duh lah nah-tah-SYOHN duh fwah par suh-MEN]
back: I go swimming twice a week.
context: 'Faire de' + activity: faire du vélo, de la danse, de la randonnée.

front: J'adore faire de la randonnée en montagne.
pronunciation: [zhah-dor fehr duh lah rahn-doh-NAY ahn mohn-TAN-yuh]
back: I love hiking in the mountains.
context: France has thousands of kilometers of marked trails (GR, 'grande randonnée').

front: Tu fais du sport ?
back: Do you do any sports?
context: 'Faire du sport' = to exercise or do sports in general.

front: Je vais à la salle de sport après le travail.
pronunciation: [zhuh veh ah lah sal duh SPOR ah-preh luh trah-VAHY]
back: I go to the gym after work.
context: 'La salle de sport' or 'la salle (de muscu)' = gym.

front: Je suis fan de cinéma.
back: I'm a movie buff.
context: 'Être fan de' = to be a fan of. 'Un cinéphile' = a film lover.

front: On va voir un film ce soir ?
pronunciation: [ohn vah vwahr an FEELM suh SWAHR]
back: Shall we go see a film tonight?
context: 'VO' (version originale) = original language with subtitles; 'VF' = dubbed in French.

front: J'écoute beaucoup de musique en travaillant.
back: I listen to a lot of music while working.
context: 'En' + present participle = while doing (gérondif).

front: Quel genre de musique tu aimes ?
back: What kind of music do you like?
context: 'Le genre' = genre, type. Answer: 'J'aime le rap, le jazz, la chanson française…'

front: Je lis surtout des romans policiers.
back: I mostly read crime novels.
context: 'Un roman' = novel; 'un roman policier' or 'un polar' = crime novel.

front: La bande dessinée est très populaire en France et en Belgique.
pronunciation: [lah bahnd day-see-NAY eh treh poh-pü-LEHR ahn frahns ay ahn bel-ZHEEK]
back: Comics are very popular in France and Belgium.
context: 'La BD' (bande dessinée) is called the 'ninth art'. Think Tintin and Astérix.

front: J'aime bien cuisiner pour mes amis.
back: I like cooking for my friends.
context: 'Aimer bien' = to like (softer than 'aimer', which with people means to love).

front: Je prends des cours de guitare.
back: I'm taking guitar lessons.
context: 'Prendre des cours' = to take lessons/classes.

front: Le week-end, je fais souvent la grasse matinée.
pronunciation: [luh wee-KEND, zhuh feh soo-vahn lah gras mah-tee-NAY]
back: On weekends, I often sleep in.
context: 'Faire la grasse matinée' (a fat morning) = to sleep in.

front: On joue aux cartes ou à un jeu de société ?
pronunciation: [ohn zhoo oh KART oo ah an zhuh duh soh-syay-TAY]
back: Shall we play cards or a board game?
context: 'Un jeu de société' = board game; 'un jeu vidéo' = video game.

front: Je suis nul en sport !
back: I'm hopeless at sports!
context: 'Être nul en' = to be bad at; 'être fort en' = to be good at.

front: Il s'entraîne pour un marathon.
back: He's training for a marathon.
context: 'S'entraîner' = to train. 'L'entraînement' = training.

front: Tu regardes le match ce soir ?
back: Are you watching the game tonight?
context: 'Regarder' = to watch. 'Les Bleus' = the French national teams.

front: Allez les Bleus !
back: Go France!
context: The cheer for French national teams, named after their blue jerseys.

front: Je fais partie d'une chorale.
back: I'm in a choir.
context: 'Faire partie de' = to be part of, belong to.

front: Le dimanche, on se balade au bord de la Seine.
pronunciation: [luh dee-MAHNSH, ohn suh bah-LAD oh bor duh lah SEN]
back: On Sundays, we go for a walk along the Seine.
context: 'Se balader' = to stroll (informal); 'se promener' is more neutral.

front: J'ai horreur des réseaux sociaux.
back: I hate social media.
context: 'Avoir horreur de' = to hate, can't stand.

front: Ça te dit d'aller au concert samedi ?
pronunciation: [sah tuh DEE dah-lay oh kohn-SEHR sahm-DEE]
back: Do you fancy going to the concert on Saturday?
context: 'Ça te dit de…?' = do you feel like…? Very common way to suggest something.

front: Je préfère la plage à la montagne.
pronunciation: [zhuh pray-fehr lah PLAZH ah lah mohn-TAN-yuh]
back: I prefer the beach to the mountains.
context: 'Préférer A à B' = to prefer A to B.

front: Mon passe-temps préféré, c'est la photographie.
back: My favorite hobby is photography.
context: 'Un passe-temps' = a hobby.

front: Je collectionne les vieux vinyles.
back: I collect old vinyl records.
context: 'Collectionner' = to collect (as a hobby).

front: On fait un pique-nique au parc ?
back: Shall we have a picnic in the park?
context: A favorite French summer activity: baguette, cheese, wine.

front: Je m'intéresse à l'histoire de l'art.
back: I'm interested in art history.
context: 'S'intéresser à' = to be interested in.

front: Le musée est gratuit le premier dimanche du mois.
pronunciation: [luh mü-ZAY eh grah-TWEE luh pruh-myay dee-MAHNSH dü MWAH]
back: The museum is free on the first Sunday of the month.
context: Many French national museums have free days. Under-26 EU residents often get in free.

front: J'ai commencé à apprendre le français l'année dernière.
pronunciation: [zhay koh-mahn-SAY ah ah-prahn-druh luh frahn-SEH lah-nay dehr-NYEHR]
back: I started learning French last year.
context: 'Commencer à' + infinitive = to start doing.

front: Je n'ai jamais le temps de lire.
pronunciation: [zhuh neh zhah-meh luh tahn duh LEER]
back: I never have time to read.
context: 'Ne… jamais' = never. 'Avoir le temps de' = to have time to.

front: On se retrouve au café après le cinéma ?
pronunciation: [ohn suh ruh-troov oh kah-FAY ah-preh luh see-nay-MAH]
back: Shall we meet at the café after the movie?
context: 'Se retrouver' = to meet up (by arrangement).

front: Ce qui me détend le plus, c'est jardiner.
pronunciation: [suh kee muh day-TAHN luh PLÜS, seh zhar-dee-NAY]
back: What relaxes me most is gardening.
context: 'Ce qui… c'est…' = what… is… A natural way to emphasize.
